subject: Simulating Occupancy/Abundance for Sites that are Spatially Autocorrelated

messages.author: 7e5b5ac76117f50b
messages.subject: Simulating Occupancy/Abundance for Sites that are Spatially Autocorrelated
parts:
I am working with data from a camera survey conducted on a sample of wildlife openings available on a wildlife management area. The sites used for the camera survey were spaced so that an individual would be unlikely to be observed at two different sites during the survey period. Using the models generated from Unmarked on this data set, I am now trying to simulate a occupancy/density estimate for every wildlife opening across the management area. From this I hope to generate a WMA wide average of occupancy and density.

The issue I am running into is that the spacing of these openings is variable and there will be a potential for spatial auto correlation between wildlife openings. Openings that are within a certain range of other openings would have a probability of having the same individuals on each. And this probability would change depending on how close two given wildlife openings are to each other. When I average across the entire WMA, these openings are biasing my estimates by overemphasizing the areas with concentrated wildlife openings.

I have read Hines et al. 2010 and other papers discussing spatial autocorrelation in Occupancy, but they emphasize dealing with spatial autocorrelation in the initial analysis of occupancy. I haven't found much discussion on how to incorporate it into simulations, especially when there was no autocorrelation to generate the models. If anyone has any experience dealing with a problem like this or can point me in the right direction, I'd really appreciate it. Thanks!

messages.author: 3d5c753ab9984eeb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Simulating Occupancy/Abundance for Sites that are Spatially Autocorrelated
parts:
Hi Matthew


1. Your description seems to contradict itself ("sites used for the camera survey were spaced so that an individual would be unlikely to be observed at two different sites" vs "Openings that are within a certain range of other openings would have a probability of having the same individuals"). Do you expect autocorrelation for other reasons?

2. I suggest this is best handled by simulating the entire sampling process i.e. distribute animals across the landscape according to some density model, then sample from that population using some detectors (wildlife openings?). There is another package that does this.

3. I'm not sure you should expect bias, rather there will be overdispersion (inflated precision) and poor spatial coverage.

4. Your free use of "occupancy/density" has me worried. Suggest you tie this down and think about the definition of "occupancy".


Murray
